strategy.summary: Reproduce the homomorphic minimum_phase Nyquist-bin mask bug in scipy.signal by building scipy at the buggy commit d2a1c1ce1f2e, applying the PR's test_nyquist test, and running it there and at the fixed revision. The defect is pure Python/numpy logic in scipy/signal/_fir_filter_design.py, so the transition should not depend on the BLAS backend. The context documents no version constraints for any dependency; numpy 1.23.5 and scipy 1.15.2 come only from the issue#22752 build header and are treated as observed versions, not documented requirements. The test compares |rfft(h)| against |rfft(minimum_phase(h))| with atol 1e-5 for float32 and 1e-13 for float64, over N in (963, 964).

build_commands: git clone https://github.com/scipy/scipy.git && cd scipy && git checkout d2a1c1ce1f2e && git submodule update --init
pip install -r requirements/build.txt (or the pip_packages above), then pip install -e . --no-build-isolation

apply the test diff from PR 24749 to scipy/signal/tests/test_fir_filter_design.py on the buggy checkout (add rfft import and the test_nyquist method inside the minimum_phase test class after test_hilbert)

after the buggy run: git stash the test, checkout the PR fixed commit (hash not given in context), rebuild with pip install -e . --no-build-isolation, reapply the test diff, and rerun the same command
pinned_because: numpy 1.23.5: observed in issue#22752 build header; no documented constraint in the context, so this is an observed-era choice; if the current main fails to build against it, use the newest numpy that builds on Python 3.10 and record that substitution
scipy-openblas32: context says OpenBLAS 0.3.28 detected via pkgconfig; provides the BLAS/LAPACK used in the build but is not involved in the defect's logic

Cython 3.0.12, pythran 0.17.0, pybind11 2.13.6: versions from issue#22752 compilers and build dependencies list; no documented constraint, so they are era-observed and may be replaced by whatever the build at d2a1c1ce1f2e requires
array-api-extra (xpx): unbounded in context; needed because the fix uses xpx.at and the test uses xp fixtures; install latest compatible version

strategy.reproducing_test: scipy/signal/tests/test_fir_filter_design.py::test_nyquist parametrized over N in (963, 964) and dtype in (float32, float64), using firwin(N, 10, window=hann, fs=100), minimum_phase(h, method=homomorphic, n_fft=N, half=False), then comparing |rfft(h,N)| with |rfft(h_min,N)| via xp_assert_close against zeros with atol 1e-5 (float32) or 1e-13 (float64).
strategy.success_criterion: On the buggy revision d2a1c1ce1f2e with the test diff applied, at least one test_nyquist case (expected the odd N=963 cases, especially float32) must FAIL because the magnitude error between the original and minimum-phase filters exceeds atol; on the fixed revision (the PR head, with win[stop] = 1 + (n_fft % 2) and win built with h_temp.dtype) all four test_nyquist cases must PASS. The transition is FAIL on buggy and PASS on fixed for the odd-length case.
strategy.numerical_probe: Compute max(abs(|rfft(h,N)| - |rfft(h_min,N)|)) for N=963 float32 and float64 on both revisions. The buggy value should be above 1e-5 for float32 and above 1e-13 for float64; the fixed value should be below both thresholds. This probe is diagnostic only; the transition is what counts.
risks: The context gives no numeric tolerance from the evidence; atol 1e-5 (float32) and 1e-13 (float64) are the values in the test diff, and the PR author says they were chosen empirically on their hardware and may need changes for CI. A different FFT or BLAS build could push the buggy or fixed error across the threshold, so the transition is not guaranteed on other machines.

The buggy error magnitude is not stated in the evidence. It is not known whether the even N=964 cases fail on the buggy revision; the transition may come only from the odd N=963 cases, so a run where every case passes on buggy means the reproduction has not been established.

numpy 1.23.5 and the other pinned-era versions are observed values from the issue header, not documented constraints. Current scipy main at d2a1c1ce1f2e may not build against numpy 1.23.5 or against the cython/pythran versions shown, which would block the buggy build before the test can run.

The fixed-commit hash is not in the context. The fixed revision must be the PR head or merge commit, identified by checking out the commit that contains the win[stop] change; a wrong fixed revision will give a misleading transition.

The defect is not tied to a platform or sanitiser per the evidence (Python-level mask logic), so it should reproduce on x86_64 Linux without special flags. The float32 ripple visibility is stated as more evident, not as requiring a specific architecture. The CuPy xfail marker does not affect the numpy backend run.
The reproducer in issue#22752 needed torch and matplotlib; the PR reduced it to the numpy-only test above, so the torch and matplotlib dependencies should not be installed for this reproduction.

The test command selects by name with -k test_nyquist; if the test is collected under a different class in the fixed revision, pytest's -k match still works, but a renamed test would silently select nothing.

oracle.tolerance: atol=1e-5 for float32 and atol=1e-13 for float64, as written in the test diff; the PR author states these were chosen empirically
oracle.reference_source: magnitude of the original windowed ideal low-pass filter h from firwin (Hann window, fc=10, fs=100), compared against the magnitude of the minimum-phase filter from minimum_phase(method=homomorphic)
oracle.why: A minimum-phase filter should have the same magnitude response as the input filter, so the difference in |rfft| should vanish; the buggy Nyquist-bin weighting adds a bandpass ripple that exceeds the tolerance.

strategy.fails_on_buggy: On d2a1c1ce1f2e the odd-length N=963 case should produce a magnitude error from the wrong Nyquist-bin weighting (the check for even signal length is inverted). xp_assert_close compares that error against zeros with atol, so the assertion fails when the ripple exceeds atol. The buggy error magnitude is not stated in the evidence; this failure is expected from the mechanism, not measured.
strategy.passes_on_fixed: On the fixed revision the Nyquist bin is set to 1 + (n_fft % 2) and win uses h_temp.dtype with xp.real(h_temp), which removes the ripple. The magnitude error should then fall below atol for all four parametrizations, so the test passes; this is expected from the fix, not confirmed by a stated value.
